headline: EU regulatory update: CSRD Omnibus adopted, battery and forced labour guidance
summary: The EU has adopted the Omnibus Directive, confirming CSRD reporting for your company from financial year 2027. Meanwhile, battery QR code rules face pending technical specifications, and German customs issued operational guidance on forced labour. EUDR enforcement readiness also remains under Commission scrutiny.

items.title: EU adopts Omnibus Directive amending CSRD timelines and thresholds
items.what: The EU has adopted the Omnibus Directive, revising reporting scope and implementation timelines under both the CSRD and CSDDD.
items.meaning: With over 1,000 employees and €450m turnover, your company falls into the revised CSRD reporting scope starting in financial year 2027.
items.action: Align sustainability reporting frameworks and supplier data requests with the revised ESRS requirements for FY2027.

sources.title: European Union adopts Omnibus Directive amending CSRD and CS3D

items.title: Battery QR code deadline set for 2027 amidst missing rulebook
items.what: Reports indicate the EU maintains a 2027 deadline for mandatory battery QR codes, even though detailed secondary technical specifications remain unfinalised.
items.meaning: Directly impacts your proprietary battery platform; system architecture and product labelling must prepare for digital passport rules.
items.action: Audit supplier capabilities for battery data management and monitor EU publication of technical implementing rules.

sources.title: Brussels Sets a 2027 Deadline for Battery QR Codes — but Its Own Rulebook Is Still Missing

items.title: German customs issues guide on EU Forced Labour Regulation
items.what: German customs published compliance guidance outlining enforcement procedures and importer expectations under the EU Forced Labour Regulation.
items.meaning: Relevant for imports from your Chinese suppliers, as customs authorities established operational procedures to inspect risk-exposed supply chains.
items.action: Strengthen supply chain tracing and labour audit documentation across all mainland China manufacturing partners.

sources.title: EU Forced Labour Regulation Germany: Zoll Guide

items.title: Commission opens infringement cases against four states over EUDR enforcement
items.what: The European Commission launched legal proceedings against four member states for failing to designate national authorities to enforce deforestation rules.
items.meaning: National enforcement readiness varies, but the 30 December 2026 application date for large operators remains unchanged.
items.action: Ensure due diligence workflows cover timber handles or paper packaging imported with finished goods.

sources.title: EU opens EUDR enforcement-authority cases against four member states
EU presses four member states to set up deforestation law enforcement before rules apply
